tb21_profile.skill: Stand up a multi-component service stack from a written spec: SSH+password auth, a bare Git repo whose post-receive hook checks out two different branches to two document roots, and an HTTPS server with a self-signed cert, all working end to end within a latency budget
tb21_profile.domain: Linux service administration - OpenSSH server, Git server and hooks, Nginx (or equivalent) TLS vhost, openssl self-signed certificates, git --work-tree branch deployment
tb21_profile.task_form: configure-a-service / build-a-pipeline from spec, verified by an external end-to-end clone-push-fetch test

notes: TMax is very deep for this query: at least a dozen tasks combine a bare repo, a post-receive hook and a TLS server on 8443, so the honest final top 10 is 8 TMax entries; I added the two non-TMax entries that cover requirements TMax does not (password-authenticated sshd, tw_11181) and cert generation validated by serving. No task anywhere in the pool deploys two branches to two different document roots - that combination is unique to TB2.1 - so nothing scored 5 on task_form except the three full pipeline builds. SWE-Smith and SWE-Rebench have no service-configuration tasks at all; theirs are scored on the narrow skill of getting a server to bind, start and serve correctly (gunicorn/daphne/starlette, aiohttp TLS knobs), and none should rank above a TMax pipeline task. The RTS shortlist was mostly the kodekloud 'add a remote and push' family plus LAMP provisioning; I kept the best of each rather than duplicates.
